sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Guard that blocks the migrate command
sections.what: Stops the migrate command before anything touches the database, and prints a message explaining how to apply SQL by hand. It also throws when DATABASE_URL is not set.
sections.why: The comments say the live database was built by hand, so running the automatic migration could cause harm.
sections.watch_out: It only catches the exact word migrate, and a command that names migrate in another argument (such as generate --name migrate) is blocked as a side effect.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Settings for the database tool
sections.what: Tells the tool where the schema code lives, where migration files go, which database type to use, and which address to connect to.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the tool generate and push changes against the right database and files.
sections.watch_out: Migration files must be read by journal index, not by timestamp, according to the comment, because the timestamps are out of order.

summary: Configuration for the Drizzle database tool. It blocks the migrate command on purpose and points the tool at the schema and the migrations folder.
purpose: Stops anyone from running the automatic migration command, which could re-apply old migrations to a live database, and tells the tool where the schema and database are.
why: The comments explain it: the live database was built by hand with psql, so the migration files are a record, not a safe command to run.
how: First, it checks the command arguments for the exact word migrate and stops with a long message explaining the manual procedure. Second, it checks that the DATABASE_URL environment variable is set. Third, it returns the settings: the schema file, the migrations output folder, the PostgreSQL dialect, and the database address from DATABASE_URL.
inputs: Command line arguments, the DATABASE_URL environment variable, and the schema file src/schema/index.ts.
outputs: A settings object for drizzle-kit. It throws an error if migrate is used or if DATABASE_URL is missing.
risks: The guard matches the exact word only, so a different command path that avoids that word would not be blocked. The guard depends on the comments and on people reading them. Editing a migration already recorded in the ledger silently breaks its stored fingerprint.
debug: If you see the DISABLED message, that is intended: apply SQL by hand. If you see the DATABASE_URL message, set that variable. For push or generate problems, check that the schema path resolves.
